evidence: I built a requirement-to-criterion map from instruction.md and the three /instructions notes against all 27 criteria (16 functional, 5 polish, 4 visual, 2 gates). Nearly every asked-for behavior is graded, mostly with positive controls. Client scope and sign-out: signin_and_client_scope. Wall by list, search, snippet, thread, transcript and direct address: wall_every_route. Wall via mentions and pasted links: wall_mentions_and_links. Live wall add and lift, and partner-only lift: wall_added_live. Three-level replies in parent order with quotes: nested_replies. Deleted-parent placeholder, author delete and the exact 7-day boundary: deleted_and_expired_messages. Shortening, turning off and partner-only timer changes with version purge: timer_changes. Hold scope, partner-only, no delete, release applies the timer, typed 'On hold': hold_scope_and_release. Edited mark, staff earlier versions, stale-edit refusal that keeps the typed text: edits_and_stale_edit. Safe formatting in thread, quote, snippet, earlier version and transcript: safe_formatting plus E1 leg 1. Message-link preview and not-available: message_links. Per-person and cross-tab unread, new-messages line, mark unread, deleted messages not counted: unread_and_new_messages_line. Idempotent send and fixed-clock order everywhere: sent_once_in_order. Live updates that keep the draft, scroll and open reply: live_updates_keep_my_work. Case-insensitive search, click-to-message, no earlier versions, full transcript contract: search_and_transcript. Restart keeps replies, edits, versions, holds, deletions, timers, walls and unread with no re-import: persistence. Polish covers the timer beside the title, the hold mark, 390px width, transcript nesting and the in-place refusal reason. The render gate covers the sign-in-only page before sign-in. Runtime mandates (Node 22, port 3000, NODE_PATH, DB_PATH, /api/health) are template policy (template integration.md). The start-from-another-cwd rule is exercised because test.sh runs from WORKDIR /tests (tests/Dockerfile). The no-symlinks rule is enforced by test.sh lines 72-83. GAP (credible, ungraded asked-for behavior): integration.md:9 says 'Anyone who isn't signed in gets no matter, message, mention or transcript data from the server.', walls-and-retention.md:35 says '...nobody else gets one, even with its address.' and walls-and-retention.md:17 says 'The same goes for clients asking about matters that aren't theirs.' The transcript route is graded only for a walled staff member (wall_every_route legs 3-4). signin_and_client_scope Part A replays only 'the request the page makes to load its messages' when signed out. Part B replays only the posting and message-loading requests against M-12 as Gwen. No criterion opens a transcript address, or fetches mentions or search data, while signed out, and none opens another client's transcript as a client. The golden itself treats these as separate paths: server.js:43 guards /api only for boot state, and the transcript is a separate non-/api page route at server.js:488. Its explicit branch at line 493, 'if (!user) return page("Not available", ... 401)', is not exercised by any criterion. Minor Note-level gaps (not a Fail on their own): (1) The '1 day' timer option is never set positively, only in Sian's refused 1-day replay (timer_changes leg 5), so a UI offering only off/7/30 is not penalised. (2) Plain http:// links are not tested, only https. (3) The fixed clock on edits is not checked, only on new messages and transcripts. (4) 'Lengthening never brings anything back' is only indirectly covered: timer_changes leg 3 checks off, and leg 4 restores 30 days without re-checking the probate message. (5) The rule that a refusal reason stays in place is graded only for sign-in (polish refusal_in_place), not for stale-edit, hold or delete refusals. (6) 'Copy seed_data.json into /app' and 'hand it over without a database' are not graded directly. The verifier ships /assets too (task.toml artifacts), so this is acceptable for non-product handover instructions. Known false positive respected: bundling several legs into one criterion is a flow, not a gap. This is a source-coverage row: no runtime evidence is needed or claimed. I did not read other reviewers' reports or earlier rounds.
counterexample: A plausible broken app scores full functional credit on this rubric. All /api routes sit behind requireAuth middleware, but the transcript is a server-rendered page at /transcripts/:id outside /api. Its only access check is: if walls.has(req.user?.id + ':' + matter) return notAvailable(); if (req.user?.role === 'client' && !isClientOf(req.user, matter)) return notAvailable(); render(transcript). Signed out, req.user is undefined, so neither branch fires. The full M-12 transcript (heads of terms, Fenwick, authors, times) is served to anyone who has the address. A variant that checks only walls in this route gives Gwen the M-12 transcript the same way. Every graded leg still passes: the /api middleware refuses the signed-out message-loading replay, the transcript route enforces Dev's wall, and no criterion fetches a transcript signed out or as another client.
suggested_fix: In signin_and_client_scope Part A, record the M-11 transcript address while Gwen is signed in, then open it after signing out: it must show not-available with no matter title, name or message. In Part B, as Gwen, open that transcript address with M-12 as the target (a replay with another target id, which the prompt already allows) and require a plain not-available. Optionally also replay the mentions request signed out. Add a positive 1-day timer step or an http:// link check only if workload allows.
